output.brief: The rejections came from our own paperwork, not the fungicide, Lower Serra fruit or Meridane's equipment. When Meridane bookings moved to the new Tallis system on 4 Aug, the mandarin product record had been copied from avocados. It carried a 7.0°C carriage temperature instead of our 4.0°C specification. Every Meridane container after that was shipped at 7°C and failed. Every container at 4°C passed, including Coastway ones packed with Pellacor, so Pellacor is not the cause. Meridane's units held the setpoint we gave them, so a claim against them would fail. Lower Serra pallets were somewhat worse inside rejected containers, but that is not enough to justify suspending growers or withholding pay. I'm confident in the main finding (about 90%). Next steps: correct the Tallis mandarin record to 4.0°C now. Ask Meridane to reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check that compares reefer settings with the product specification before anything is submitted. Hold off on the supplier switch-back, the Lower Serra suspension and the cargo claim. Loggers are a reasonable extra safeguard.
